clue.text: Tailless monkey grabs rug right away — it's awful!

indicators.note: grabs means the monkey holds the next piece inside it
tailless means the monkey's name loses its final letter

parts.note: a baboon is a monkey

indicators.note: right away means the R (right) is taken out of rug

explanation.surface: A monkey with no tail snatches a rug, and someone cries out in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' and 'right away' are both trimming signals: one drops the monkey's last letter, the other removes R from the rug; 'grabs' then wraps one round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugaboo is a bugbear or object of dread, something felt to be awful.

clue.text: Ruth, possibly, gets one up in arms

definitions.meaning: ... Ruth, the American baseball star, possibly referred to by his nickname
a baby carried in someone's arms

explanation.surface: Ruth may end up armed and ready to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in arms' suggests anger but means held in someone's arms, like a babe in arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe was the nickname of baseball's Ruth, and a babe is an infant carried in the arms.

clue.text: Crew means to secure passage on ship

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: A crew's method of booking a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway is a passageway on a ship, or the walkway onto one.

clue.text: Promote prize possession, having change of heart

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a boast can be a thing one is proud of, a prized possession

explanation.surface: Advance a treasured item after a change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having change of heart' replaces the middle A of BOAST with O.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost something is to promote or push it.

clue.text: Accidentally learn about present declaration

parts.note: over can mean about, as in fussing over something

indicators.note: a declaration is spoken, so the word is written as it sounds

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Discover by chance something about a present being announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declaration' means HERE is spoken, and written HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhear is to catch words by chance that were not meant for you.

clue.text: Painter of some power expressed surprise, loudly

parts.note: a watt is a unit of power

indicators.note: loudly signals that the next piece is something spoken, and we write a word that sounds the same

parts.note: saying 'oh' is how one expresses surprise

explanation.surface: An artist of some force gasps in astonishment out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' means OH is heard, and it is written EAU, the French word for water, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Watteau was an eighteenth-century French painter of fêtes galantes.

clue.text: Squeeze restricting current electrical work

indicators.note: restricting means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to wring is to squeeze
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Tight budgets hamper ongoing work on the electrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiring is the system of electrical wires installed in a building, electricians' work.

clue.text: It has its ups and downs as an aid to loading

definitions.text: It has its ups and downs as an aid to loading

parts.words: It has its ups and downs as an aid to loading
parts.note: the hinged back of a lorry is raised and lowered to let goods on and off, read as if describing a fickle life

explanation.surface: Something with a chequered history helps with loading.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailboard is the hinged board at the back of a truck, lowered for loading.

clue.text: Recluse buried over in one-time refuge

indicators.note: over means the concealed letters are read backwards
buried means the letters sit concealed in the following words

explanation.surface: A hermit is laid to rest in a sanctuary of former days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried' finds ETIMERE in 'one-time refuge' and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, especially a Christian one, a recluse living alone.

clue.text: Lacking intelligence, Pole enters in regimentals

indicators.note: enters means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: regimentals are military uniform, so wearing them is being uniformed
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A dim-witted Polish man joins up in army dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person; it is N for the north pole, and 'enters' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking intelligence in the sense of information, not brains: uninformed people have not been told.

clue.text: Shoulder belt and, trunk a monarch placed outside

indicators.note: placed outside means the trunk goes round the word 'and'

parts.note: a bole is a tree trunk
taken as written
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a monarch

explanation.surface: Some odd inventory: a belt, a trunk and a sovereign put out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'and' hides that the word itself is fodder; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandoleer is a belt worn over the shoulder with loops for cartridges.

clue.text: Old people retiring in City district

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
EC1 is a postal district of the City of London, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Elderly folk leave work while living in a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: EC1 is a London postcode in the City, the digit 1 standing for the letter I; 'retiring' turns the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe, Boudicca's people, so an old people in the sense of a nation.

clue.text: For counsel it may be a lengthy observation

definitions.text: For counsel it may be a lengthy observation

parts.words: For counsel it may be a lengthy observation
parts.note: a barrister may be instructed simply to follow a case on a client's behalf, which reads cryptically as keeping a long look at something

explanation.surface: A lawyer's instructions might amount to a long spell of looking on.
explanation.definitionFit: A watching brief instructs a barrister to follow a case for an interested party without taking part, a prolonged observation.

clue.text: Standard stage clown

definitions.meaning: a criterion against which things are judged
the jester in Shakespeare's As You Like It

explanation.surface: A conventional theatrical buffoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone is a standard of quality, and Touchstone is the fool in As You Like It.

clue.text: Majestic knight leaves sole member in a flap

indicators.note: leaves means the knight's letter departs from the word for sole

parts.note: sole means only
N is the chess notation for a knight
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: in a flap means agitated, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grand knight walks out, the only parliamentarian left in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes N from ONLY to leave OLY; 'flap' rearranges IN A to IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympian describes the lofty, godlike manner of the Olympian gods, so majestic in bearing.

clue.text: Eccentric in grey cap delivers encomium

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball in a grey hat gives a speech of high praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A panegyric is a formal speech or writing of praise, which is what an encomium is.

clue.text: Occupation always connected with transport

parts.note: a car is a form of transport
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A job forever tied up with moving goods or people.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is one's profession or lifelong occupation.

clue.text: Poet and classicist carrying note for doctor

indicators.note: carrying means the poet's name holds the next piece within it

parts.note: A. E. Housman was both poet and classical scholar
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A scholarly poet bears a letter for the physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts E inside HOUSMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain, now called a foundation doctor.

clue.text: Son leaves Lieutenant outside new gambling-place

indicators.note: outside means the shortened name goes round the next piece
leaves means the son's letter is dropped from the lieutenant's name

parts.note: Cassio is Othello's lieutenant in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A son quits an army lieutenant beyond a fresh betting establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes one S from CASSIO, giving CASIO; 'outside' puts that around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building where people gamble.

clue.text: Fashionable around province, like Eumaeus's charges

indicators.note: around means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: swish means smart or fashionable
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A stylish person tours a region, much like a herd in the Odyssey.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is commonly called the Province in Britain; Eumaeus is the loyal swineherd in Homer's Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: Eumaeus is Odysseus's swineherd, so his charges are pigs, and swinish means pig-like.

clue.text: Cook is adored, by the way

indicators.note: to cook figures is to rework them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The chef is worshipped, incidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' passes for a throwaway phrase but is the definition, literally beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at the roadside is located by the way, alongside the road.

clue.text: Hint of dark fluid found on heather

parts.note: ink is a dark liquid for writing
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: A trace of black liquid discovered on a moorland plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight hint or suspicion.

clue.text: Bring about settlement of estate

definitions.meaning: a legal arrangement fixing who inherits property

explanation.surface: Arrange how an estate is to be settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve as a consequence; an entail is a settlement restricting inheritance.

clue.text: Leave sweetened drink a person mixed, perhaps

parts.note: a sling is a sweetened spirit drink, like a gin sling
one means a person
shook means mixed, as a cocktail is shaken

explanation.surface: Instructions to someone to make a sweet cocktail and shake it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the sling as one example of a sweetened drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To sling one's hook is British slang for clearing off, an idiom for leave.

clue.text: Area in huge island, a haven of peace

indicators.note: in means the area letter goes inside

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size for huge

explanation.surface: A place within a vast isle that is a refuge of calm.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing size meaning extra large.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is figuratively a pleasant refuge of calm amid hostile surroundings.

clue.text: Loveless emissary's sin?

indicators.note: love is zero, the letter O, which is removed

parts.note: an envoy is an emissary; the 's joins the parts

explanation.surface: Could it be the moral failing of an ambassador without affection?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loveless' takes O (love, zero in tennis) out of ENVOY; the question mark flags envy as one example of a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Basket material a girl put right at the back

indicators.note: the R for right is shifted to the end of the name

parts.note: Rosie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl tidies basketry supplies away at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put right at the back' moves the R of ROSIE to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is willow whose pliant shoots are used to weave baskets.

clue.text: Acknowledgment of crime for which one may be charged

definitions.text: for which one may be charged
definitions.meaning: an entry fee, the price charged to go in

explanation.surface: A confession that could get someone prosecuted.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission means both a confession and the price paid for entry somewhere.

clue.text: It's available on prescription only, confusing the laic

indicators.note: confusing the words jumbles their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A medicine restricted to prescriptions bewilders the layman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the laic' means a layperson, who might be confused by medical terms.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethical drug is one sold only on a doctor's prescription, a pharmacy term.

clue.text: Lack of influence in decision about, for example, flowers

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: having no say means lacking any voice in a decision

explanation.surface: Being powerless over a choice about, say, blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NO SAY around EG, giving NO S-EG-AY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of flowers.
